cues.zh: 都是新奇的、革命性的，

cues.zh: 而且你很可能能靠它谋生。

cues.zh: 万维网——我出生时，ARPANET 已经存在，计算机已经存在，我们已经有彩色电视

cues.zh: 以及计算机网络之类的概念。但我们现在所认识的那种互联网，当时其实还不存在。

cues.en: Things invented

The things that were invented after I turned 35 and are therefore unnatural and against the order of things are the Apple Watch,
cues.zh: 万维网大概是在我15岁左右被发明出来的。后来我确实在这一行发展得不错。我从网站管理员做起。我学了 HTML。我做过这类事情。而我35岁之后发明出来的、因此显得不自然且违背事物秩序的东西，是 Apple Watch，

cues.en: Now then, while IBM are working out how to put computers in your house, the Advanced Research Projects Agency, ARPA, is coming up with this crazy idea to connect computers together.
cues.zh: 那么，就在 IBM 琢磨怎么把电脑送进你家的时候，高级研究计划局 ARPA 正琢磨出一个疯狂的想法——把计算机连起来。

cues.en: And they had this good idea. Like, we could connect four computers together so that if one of them got wiped out by some kind of Cold War military attack, the others still work, that might be a good idea. Let's start engineering here for resilience.
cues.zh: 他们有个好点子。比如，我们可以把四台计算机连在一起，这样如果其中一台被某种冷战军事攻击摧毁了，其他的还能继续工作，这也许是个好主意。咱们就从这里开始为韧性做工程设计吧。

cues.en: And around the same time as IBM was launching the PC, ARPA published a specification for an Internetworking
cues.zh: 大约在 IBM 推出个人电脑的同时，ARPA 发布了一份互联网络规范

cues.en: protocol.
cues.zh: 协议。

cues.en: The standard, became known as IPv4, was published around 1981. This is actually a map
cues.zh: 这个标准后来被称为 IPv4，大约在 1981 年发布。这其实是一张地图

cues.en: a map of the Internet from 1973
cues.zh: 一张 1973 年的互联网地图

cues.en: of every single device that was connected to the ARPANET before it became the Internet. Drawn by hand, by a draftsperson with a pen and paper, that's every single device and what they're running.
cues.zh: 展示了在 ARPANET 变成互联网之前，连接到上面的每一个设备。这是由绘图员用纸和笔手绘的，每一个设备以及它们运行的程序都在上面。

cues.en: This was published in 1981. 01/01/1983
cues.zh: 这是在 1981 年发布的。1983 年 1 月 1 日

cues.en: became known as Flag Day. That was the day they said, from now on, everything connected to our network must run TCPIP.
cues.zh: 被称为“标志日”（Flag Day）。那是他们宣布的日子：从今以后，连接到我们网络的所有设备都必须运行 TCP/IP。

cues.en: That's it. 1982,
cues.zh: 就是这样。1982 年，

cues.en: they ratified a standard called SMTP,
cues.zh: 他们批准了一个名为 SMTP 的标准，

cues.en: the Simple Mail Transfer Protocol.
cues.zh: 即简单邮件传输协议。

cues.en: We suddenly had this system where all the computers in the world could talk to each other and a system where the people using those computers could send mail to one another.
cues.zh: 我们突然拥有了这样一个系统：世界上所有的计算机都可以互相通信，使用这些计算机的人也可以互相发送邮件。

cues.en: Now,
cues.zh: 现在，

cues.en: the Internet started to grow.
cues.zh: 互联网开始增长。

cues.en: And the problem with systems that are growing is you need a way of keeping track of them. Now, there are only two really hard problems in computer science. One of them is cache invalidation. The other one is naming things.
cues.zh: 而不断增长的系统所带来的问题是，你需要一种方法来跟踪它们。现在，计算机科学中真正只有两个难题。一个是缓存失效。另一个是命名。

cues.en: So let's talk about DNS.
cues.zh: 所以我们来谈谈 DNS。

cues.en: Because before DNS was invented,
cues.zh: 因为在 DNS 发明之前，

cues.en: if you set up a new server and you put it on the Internet, you would plug it in.
cues.zh: 如果你搭建了一台新服务器并把它接入互联网，你把它插上电。

cues.en: And then you would phone Jake and you would say, Jake,
cues.zh: 然后你会打电话给 Jake 并说，Jake，

cues.en: I've got a new computer. Can you add it to the host's file, please?
cues.zh: 我有一台新电脑。能把它加到 hosts 文件里吗？

cues.en: This was the host's file. It was a file that lived at the network information center at Stanford.
cues.zh: 这是主机的文件。这个文件存放在斯坦福的网络信息中心。

cues.en: And when one of your team was going there for a meeting, you'd say, oh, can you grab a copy of the host's file and bring it back? Or you'd FTP it overnight when the phone calls were cheap or you'd get them to send you a copy on a tape or something. But this was how
cues.zh: 当你团队里有人要去那儿开会时，你会说，哦，你能顺便拿一份主机文件的副本带回来吗？或者你会趁夜里电话费便宜的时候用FTP传过来，或者让他们用磁带什么的给你寄一份。但这就是

cues.en: organizations
cues.zh: 各个组织

cues.en: managed their list of hosts that were connected to the internet with this one file. If you wanted to add a machine to the host's file on a public holiday, you couldn't because the people who had permission to edit the file were all off celebrating with their families. You couldn't add machines at night or on the weekend or at Thanksgiving or at Christmas.
cues.zh: 用这一个文件来管理它们连接到互联网的主机列表的方式。如果你想在公共假日往主机文件里添加一台机器，你做不到，因为有权限编辑这个文件的人都休假回家过节了。你没法在夜里、周末、感恩节或圣诞节添加机器。

cues.en: And it kind of worked for a while, but it was obvious that this internet thing was likely to start growing a little bit and maybe we needed a better system.
cues.zh: 这凑合着用了一阵子，但很明显，这个互联网东西很可能会开始增长一点，也许我们需要一个更好的系统。

cues.en: Enter this guy. That's Paul Mocupetres.
cues.zh: 这位登场了。这是Paul Mocupetres。

cues.en: He's from the University of Southern California, which also invented Unix and LSD.
cues.zh: 他来自南加州大学，这所大学还发明了Unix和LSD。

cues.en: So thank you, University of SoCal, for those contributions to society.
cues.zh: 所以感谢南加州大学对社会做出的这些贡献。

cues.en: And they hired him and they said, look, we need a better thing, better solution to this host system. We've these five different engineering solutions.
cues.zh: 他们雇了他，说，你看，我们需要一个更好的东西，更好的方案来解决这个主机系统的问题。我们有这五种不同的工程方案。

cues.en: Could you look at them all and just pick the best ones and keep everyone happy? Now,
cues.zh: 你能不能都看一下，挑出最好的，让大家都满意？然后，

cues.en: I quite like what he did next because I think it's what I would have done next. He looked at all five of these solutions and went, these are all crap, and threw them away.
cues.zh: 我挺喜欢他接下来的做法，因为我觉得换我我也会这么干。他看了这五个方案，说，这些都是垃圾，然后把它们全扔了。

cues.en: And he
cues.zh: 而他

cues.en: designed and invented by himself DNS,
cues.zh: 亲自设计并发明了 DNS，

cues.en: a hierarchical
cues.zh: 这是一个分层的

cues.en: database of host names and network addresses,
cues.zh: 主机名与网络地址数据库，

cues.en: which has the fantastic quality. It has survived
cues.zh: 它具备一项奇妙的特质。它历经沧桑

cues.en: pretty much unchanged from his original specification
cues.zh: 几乎完全沿用了他最初的规范，

cues.en: because he designed it to scale with the complexity of the network it was supporting.
cues.zh: 因为他在设计时就考虑到了要随其所支持的网络复杂度一起扩展。

cues.en: The more hosts you connect, the more DNS servers you've got, the more you can share the load. The more stuff gets cached. The fewer root level lookups actually have to happen to make that system work. And that still survives today, supporting
cues.zh: 你连接的主机越多，拥有的 DNS 服务器越多，就能分担越多负载。缓存的内容也越多。让这个系统正常运转实际所需的根级别查询就越少。而这一切至今犹存，如今正支撑着

cues.en: hundreds of millions of domains now.
cues.zh: 数以亿计的域名。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: the scene is set. TCPIP
cues.zh: 舞台已经搭好。TCP/IP

cues.en: exists. DNS exists. SMTP exists. We've got conventions and protocols.
cues.zh: 存在。DNS 存在。SMTP 存在。我们有了各种约定和协议。

cues.en: Computer hardware, commodity hardware is cheap. Lots of people have it.
cues.zh: 计算机硬件，即商用硬件变得很便宜。很多人都拥有它。

cues.en: And in CERN, on the border of France and Switzerland,
cues.zh: 而在位于法国和瑞士边境的欧洲核子研究中心（CERN），

cues.en: this guy, Tim Berners Lee,
cues.zh: 这个人，蒂姆·伯纳斯-李（Tim Berners-Lee），

cues.en: web developer,
cues.zh: 网页开发者，

cues.en: is
cues.zh: 他

cues.en: he actually he uses this job title. That's the real title that Tim Berners Lee uses.
cues.zh: 其实他用的就是这个职位头衔。这就是蒂姆·伯纳斯-李实际使用的头衔。

cues.en: And I love Scott Hansolman's like, he could have been the web developer.
cues.zh: 我特别喜欢 Scott Hanselman 说的，他本来可以被称为“那个网页开发者”。

cues.en: But he's like, no, web developer's fine.
cues.zh: 但他觉得，不，网页开发者挺好的。

cues.en: He's working at CERN. And he's
cues.zh: 他在 CERN 工作。并且他

cues.en: noticed they have these fantastic computer networks now. But most of his colleagues who are physicists and mathematicians,
cues.zh: 注意到他们现在有了这些棒极了的计算机网络。但他的大多数同事都是物理学家和数学家，

cues.en: if they want to publish their work so someone else can read it, they don't really have a kind of digital equivalent of journals.
cues.zh: 如果他们想发表自己的研究成果以便别人阅读，其实并没有某种数字版的期刊替代品。

cues.en: And he thinks, what if we could come up with a way of publishing material
cues.zh: 他认为，如果能想出办法来发布材料呢

cues.en: online, on the network?
cues.zh: 在线，在网络上？

cues.en: So he writes up a proposal, information management, Tim Berners Lee. And he sends it to his supervisor,
cues.zh: 于是他写了一份提案，信息管理，Tim Berners Lee。然后他把它发给他的主管，

cues.en: who sends it back with a three word comment.
cues.zh: 主管退回来时附了三个词的评论。

cues.en: Vague,
cues.zh: 含糊，

cues.en: but exciting.
cues.zh: 但令人兴奋。

cues.en: Now
cues.zh: 现在

cues.en: it is really easy in hindsight to think, well, obviously that's the World Wide Web. That's how it was going to end up, this idea of HTML and HTTP and links and all this kind of stuff. I was studying at the University of Southampton in 1997.
cues.zh: 事后看来真的很容易想，嗯，显然那就是万维网。事情注定会发展成那样，HTML和HTTP、链接之类的想法。1997年我在南安普顿大学读书。

cues.en: And one of my professors actually two of my professors there had
cues.zh: 我的一位教授，实际上那里的两位教授

cues.en: worked on a competing submission for hypermedia before the World Wide Web was invented. There was this big international hypermedia conference
cues.zh: 在万维网发明之前，曾参与过一个竞争性的超媒体提交方案。有一个大型国际超媒体会议

cues.en: and one of my professors, he said, sat there and I got up and I showed them my system. And then the next guy who got up was this chap called Tim who had come over from CERN. And I sat there and I thought, yeah, we're not going to get this one.
cues.zh: 我的一位教授，他说，坐在那儿，我站起来向他们展示了我的系统。然后下一个站起来的是这位叫Tim的家伙，他是从CERN过来的。我坐在那儿想，是啊，这个我们赢不了。

cues.en: But the system that the Southampton team had was a thing called Microcosm.
cues.zh: 但南安普顿团队的系统叫做Microcosm。

cues.en: And this is actually a screenshot of a running Microcosm system running on Windows 3.1.
cues.zh: 这实际上是一个运行在Windows 3.1上的Microcosm系统的截图。

cues.en: And Microcosm
cues.zh: 而Microcosm

cues.en: didn't use embedded hypermedia because their philosophy is we don't want people to have to edit their documents.
cues.zh: 没有使用嵌入式超媒体，因为他们的理念是，我们不想让人们不得不编辑自己的文档。

cues.en: Because these documents already exist, we don't want to have to rewrite everything. What we'll do is we'll invent a network server that can maintain a database of links independently of the material that's being linked.
cues.zh: 因为这些文档已经存在了，我们不想重写一切。我们要做的是发明一个网络服务器，它可以独立于被链接的材料来维护一个链接数据库。

cues.en: So you can put your text files and your rich text files and your WordPerfect files and whatever on a network file share. And we will run indexing service over the top of them that doesn't touch the original documents, but it looks for keywords and contexts. And it links things into other things. And it shows you all of the links here in a separate window running alongside your content so that you're always presenting the original document the way the author intended it to be done and the hypermedia is being applied by
cues.zh: 你可以把文本文件、富文本文件、WordPerfect 文件等等放在网络文件共享上。然后我们在它们之上运行索引服务，不改动原始文档，而是查找关键词和上下文。它会把事物相互链接起来。并在与你的内容并排运行的单独窗口中显示所有这些链接，这样你始终按作者原本意图呈现原始文档，而超媒体则由

cues.en: librarians and information analysts.
cues.zh: 图书管理员和信息分析师来应用。

cues.en: And it's fascinating just to see this now has survived. Microcosm became Multicosm PLC,
cues.zh: 看到这个如今还存活着，真是令人着迷。Microcosm 变成了 Multicosm PLC，

cues.en: who now do a very good line doing
cues.zh: 他们现在有一块很不错的业务，做

cues.en: discovery and big lawsuits where they've got all these documents and files on some company's subpoenaed server.
cues.zh: 发现和大型诉讼，他们拿到某公司被传唤服务器上的所有文档和文件。

cues.en: And they use a variation of that tech to this day to go through and index all that material.
cues.zh: 他们至今仍在使用那项技术的变体来梳理并索引所有那些材料。

cues.en: But this is a completely
cues.zh: 但这是关于在线超媒体

cues.en: different philosophy on how online hypermedia
cues.zh: 原本可能如何运作的一种完全

cues.en: might have worked.
cues.zh: 不同的理念。

cues.en: But
cues.zh: 但是

cues.en: You unlock this door with the key of imagination.
cues.zh: 你用想象力的钥匙打开这扇门。

cues.en: Beyond it is another dimension.
cues.zh: 门后是另一个维度。

cues.en: A dimension of sound,
cues.zh: 一个声音的维度，

cues.en: a dimension of sight,
cues.zh: 一个视觉的维度，

cues.en: a dimension of mind.
cues.zh: 一个心灵的维度。

cues.en: You're moving into a land of both shadow and substance, of things and ideas.
cues.zh: 你正进入一片既有阴影又有实体的土地，事物与观念并存。

cues.en: You've just crossed over into
cues.zh: 你刚刚跨入了

cues.en: the twilight zone.
cues.zh: 暮光之城。

cues.en: We're at CERN.
cues.zh: 我们在 CERN。

cues.en: It's the early 1990s. Tim Berners Lee is in his office. He's been playing around with something called the Mesh.
cues.zh: 那是 1990 年代初。Tim Berners Lee 在他的办公室里。他一直在摆弄一个叫 Mesh 的东西。

cues.en: And a couple of other people have also got projects that are related to Mesh systems and things, and he's thinking he needs a new name for it. And he has this idea, he thinks, what if I call it the World Wide Web? And he's scribbling www on pieces of paper and ideas and everything. And then something fortuitous happens one day. The network goes down. And he has to tell someone what he's doing over the phone.
cues.zh: 还有另外几个人也有一些跟网状系统相关之类的主意，然后他在想得给它起个新名字。他脑子里冒出一个想法，心想，如果我把它叫作 World Wide Web 怎么样？于是他在纸上涂涂画画写下 www 各种点子什么的。接着有一天，一件机缘巧合的事发生了。网络瘫痪了。而他必须在电话里跟别人说明他在做什么。

cues.en: And he picks the phone up because of it. And he goes, yeah, it's this this w w w. And they say, hang on a second.
cues.zh: 为此他拿起了电话。然后他说，对，就是这个 w w w。接着对方说，等一下。

cues.en: That acronym is actually longer than the thing it's short for.
cues.zh: 这个缩写其实比它简写的那几个词还要长。

cues.en: This is gonna if this catches on it, it might sound a little bit daft. And Tim thinks, you know, that's a good point. So he calls his colleagues in when they're all having tea at 04:00 in the afternoon
cues.zh: 这要是流行起来的话，听上去可能会有点傻气。Tim 一想，还真是这么回事。于是他在下午四点大家一起喝茶的时候把同事们叫了过来

cues.en: and says, look, I've got this thing and I need some names for it. What do you think? And someone goes, yeah, well, World Wide Web, yeah, I see the problem with that one. What if we call it the International Information Interchange,
cues.zh: 然后说，听着，我搞出了这么个东西，得给它起几个名字。你们觉得呢？然后有人说，行吧，World Wide Web，嗯，我也觉得这个名字有问题。如果我们把它叫作 International Information Interchange 怎么样，

cues.en: the I I I? And someone goes, no, that sounds like pirates.
cues.zh: 也就是 I I I？接着有人说，不对，听起来像海盗。

cues.en: And someone who's just read Neuromancer says, what about the multinational metadata matrix?
cues.zh: 然后有个刚读过《神经漫游者》的人说，叫 multinational metadata matrix 怎么样？

cues.en: And they think, oh, yeah, that sounds like it could have potential. They play around with these ideas for a little while. Eventually he comes up with the global repository of interlinked documents,
cues.zh: 他们一想，哦，对，这个听起来挺有潜力的。他们琢磨了一会儿这些点子。最后他想出了一个名字：global repository of interlinked documents，

cues.en: the grid.
cues.zh: 也就是 grid。

cues.en: He's got a name. He needs a protocol.
cues.zh: 他有了名字，还需要一个协议。

cues.en: Protocols are always called the something, something, something transfer protocol, file transfer protocol, mail transfer protocol. He's like, I'm slinging hypertext here, hypertext transfer protocol.
cues.zh: 协议总是叫某某某传输协议，文件传输协议、邮件传输协议。他心想，我这儿传的是超文本，那就叫超文本传输协议。

cues.en: And he looks around and thinks, well, there's a couple of basic operations for publishing and updating documents.
cues.zh: 他环顾四周，琢磨着，发布和更新文档无非就几个基本操作。

cues.en: And he looks at structured query language, SQL. And he thinks, we can borrow some ideas from that. We'll have a verb in our thing, select, means select that document from that server, bring it back to me. Create,
cues.zh: 他看了看结构化查询语言，SQL，心想可以借鉴一些思路。我们的协议里也要有个动词，select，意思是从那台服务器上选中那个文档，给我取回来。Create，

cues.en: I want to publish something on the grid.
cues.zh: 我想在网格上发布点东西。

cues.en: Update, I made a mistake. Please take that document and update it with these changes. Delete means take that down. The lawyers have just got in touch and that's not supposed to be there.
cues.zh: Update，我搞错了，请把那个文档拿去，用这些改动更新一下。Delete 就是撤下来，律师刚联系过，那东西不该在那儿。

cues.en: And someone walks into his office and goes, you know, maybe
cues.zh: 有人走进他办公室说，你知道吗，也许

cues.en: it's just possible it might end up supporting more than that.
cues.zh: 它有可能最终支持的不止这些。

cues.en: What if we add submit as well so you can send instructions to a remote system, get it to do something for you? Now one of the things that Tim really likes about these is they're all the same length. So when you view your web log files sorry, your grid log files in a fixed width font, it all lines up nicely. Wouldn't that sound like a nice engineering solution?
cues.zh: 要是再加个 submit 呢，这样你就能给远程系统发指令，让它替你干活。Tim 特别喜欢的一点是，这些动词长度都一样。所以当你用等宽字体查看 web 日志文件——抱歉，是网格日志文件时，全都对得整整齐齐。这听起来不就是个漂亮的工程方案吗？

cues.en: The next thing they need, we've got a protocol, we've got a name, we've got all these resources, these grid pages that are going to be out there on the Internet somewhere. We need a way of identifying
cues.zh: 接下来他们需要的——协议有了，名字有了，还有所有这些资源，这些网格页面将来会放在互联网的某处。我们需要一种方式来标识

cues.en: the ones we're looking at, the thing we want to select.
cues.zh: 我们正在看的那些，我们想选中的那个东西。

cues.en: He plays around for a little while. He comes up with something that becomes the standard unique resource finder.
cues.zh: 他玩了一会儿。然后想出了一个后来成为标准唯一资源查找器的东西。

cues.en: The word surf looks like it might catch on. People might talk about surfing the grid. That could be interesting.
cues.zh: “surf”这个词看起来可能会流行起来。人们可能会谈论“冲浪网格（surfing the grid）”。那可能挺有意思。

cues.zh: 但是，

cues.zh: 他也并不是唯一一位在 Apple 任职后离开的远见卓识的工程师。

cues.en: There's a startup,
cues.zh: 有一家初创公司，

cues.en: B Incorporated.
cues.zh: Be Incorporated。

cues.en: B have a thing called the BIOS.
cues.zh: Be 打造了一个叫 BeOS 的系统。

cues.en: It is a completely
cues.zh: 这是一个完全

cues.en: brand new ground up high performance operating system. It has dedicated threading support for playing streaming media, doing real time communication, audio processing, all these kinds of things.
cues.zh: 从零构建的高性能全新操作系统。它具备专门的线程支持，用于流媒体播放、实时通信、音频处理等各种场景。

cues.en: And what Bee have realized
cues.zh: 而 Be 意识到的是，

cues.en: is their operating system is fantastic,
cues.zh: 他们的操作系统非常出色，

cues.en: but the boxes, the physical computers they were building to run it on,
cues.zh: 但他们自己制造的、用来运行该系统的实体电脑硬件，

cues.en: those are proving really difficult to pin down. So they have pivoted.
cues.zh: 却困难重重、难以落地。于是他们调整了方向。

cues.en: They've changed their strategy. They are going to try and find hardware.
cues.zh: 他们改变了策略，打算去寻找外部硬件。

cues.en: And their first step, because both of the engineers behind it have an Apple background,
cues.zh: 而他们的第一步，因为背后的两位工程师都有 Apple 背景，

cues.en: is to port BIOS onto Apple hardware.
cues.zh: 就是将 BeOS 移植到 Apple 硬件上。

cues.en: They set up a meeting. They go and see the Apple people and they say,
cues.zh: 他们安排了一次会面，前去拜访 Apple 的人并表示：

cues.en: we've got this brilliant high performance multi threaded
cues.zh: 我们研发出了这样一款极其出色、高性能、多线程、

cues.en: real mode protected mode operating system. Would you be interested
cues.zh: 兼具实模式与保护模式的操作系统。你们是否有兴趣

cues.en: in acquiring
cues.zh: 收购

cues.en: it? And Apple think this is brilliant. This is exactly the thing that they've been looking for.
cues.zh: 它？Apple 觉得这太棒了，这正是他们梦寐以求的东西。

cues.en: They jump all in. They love the styling. They love the branding. They love it so much that the next line of Apple computers that come out,
cues.zh: 他们全力投入。他们喜欢它的外观设计，喜欢它的品牌风格。喜欢到 Apple 随后推出的下一代电脑产品，

cues.en: which are instantly dubbed banana boxes by the press,
cues.zh: 立刻被媒体戏称为“香蕉盒”。

cues.en: These things are brilliant. Up till now, computers have been gray and beige. Suddenly they can make them in yellow? No one had ever thought of doing this before. Imagine a computer that wasn't beige. People want this in their house.
cues.zh: 这些产品太惊艳了。在此之前，电脑一直都是灰色和米黄色的。突然间竟然能做成黄色的？以前从没人想过这么干。想象一下摆脱米黄色的电脑，大家都想在家里摆上一台。

cues.en: It's beautiful. It's running this amazing new BIOS operating system. The one thing they don't have
cues.zh: 很漂亮。它运行着这个惊人的新BIOS操作系统。他们唯一没有的

cues.en: is a grid browser.
cues.zh: 这是一个网格浏览器。

cues.en: So they make a couple of phone calls and they ring the cello people and they're like, we already did the deal with Perfect Digital. You missed that one.
cues.zh: 于是他们打了几个电话，联系了大提琴那边的人，对方说，我们已经和Perfect Digital达成协议了。你们错过那一单了。

cues.en: And they ring NCSA and NCSA say, well, Mailake's kind of open source and limping along, but it's not really doing very much.
cues.zh: 然后他们打电话给 NCSA，NCSA 说，嗯，Mailake 算是开源的，而且发展步履蹒跚，但其实没做多少事。

cues.en: And then out of the blue, they phoned the Norwegian telephone company,
cues.zh: 然后他们突然给挪威电话公司打了电话，

cues.en: Telenor.
cues.zh: Telenor。

cues.en: And Telenor say, you know, this is funny. We have a grid browser we've been working on here. It's a thing we call Opera.
cues.zh: Telenor 就说，巧了，我们这边一直在做一款网格浏览器，我们管它叫 Opera。

cues.en: And we're not quite sure what to do with it.
cues.zh: 我们也不太确定该怎么处理它。

cues.en: So the BIOS people and the Apple people and the Norwegian telephone company make a deal and they acquire Opera. The source code for that, the Presto rendering engine, the network stack that runs it, they rename it bLink to go with bBoxes and bUs. And of course, it instantly gets renamed to blink by autocorrect.
cues.zh: 于是BIOS的人、苹果的人和挪威电话公司达成协议，收购了Opera。收购的源代码，包括Presto渲染引擎、运行它的网络栈，他们把它改名为bLink，以配合bBoxes和bUs。当然，它立刻被自动纠错改成了blink。

cues.en: It supports all the grid protocols, create, update, delete, select, submit. It's got a WYSIWYG editor. Suddenly there is a first class competitor again to the juggernaut,
cues.zh: 它支持所有 Grid 协议，创建、更新、删除、选择、提交。它有一个所见即所得编辑器。突然间，那个巨无霸又迎来了一流的竞争对手，

cues.en: which is perfect digital running on these beige office clones.
cues.zh: 它完美地以数字化形式运行在这些米色办公克隆机上。

cues.en: Now
cues.zh: 现在

cues.en: people all over the world have got these systems and they are writing and posting grid pages left, right, and center.
cues.zh: 世界各地的人都已经用上了这些系统，正在到处编写和发布 Grid 页面。

cues.en: Everyone is getting dial up and everyone is getting five megabytes of grid space free
cues.zh: 每个人都在拨号上网，每个人都免费获得五兆的网格空间。

cues.en: when they do this. Because you can publish a lot of stuff in five megabytes because we never invented those massive JavaScript frameworks in this universe.
cues.zh: 当他们这么做时。因为你可以在五兆字节里发布很多东西，因为在这个宇宙里我们从未发明那些庞大的JavaScript框架。

cues.en: And it's becoming very, very difficult to find the good stuff because people are just putting crap online because they think if they get users, maybe later they can work out how to make money out of all of that traffic.
cues.zh: 而且现在要找到好东西变得非常非常难，因为人们只管往网上扔垃圾，他们觉得只要先拿到用户，也许以后就能想办法从这些流量里赚钱。

cues.en: And the big unsolved problem in grid computing has become, how do we find content? How do we search for the things that we want to look at?
cues.zh: 而网格计算中最大的未解问题变成了：我们怎么找到内容？怎么搜索我们想看的东西？

cues.en: Now at Stanford, there's a couple of PhD students, Sergei Page and Larry Brin.
cues.zh: 现在在斯坦福，有两个博士生，Sergei Page 和 Larry Brin。

cues.en: And they're working out of a garage on an algorithm they call Backrub.
cues.zh: 他们在车库里研究一个算法，叫 Backrub。

cues.en: And they call it Backrub because it uses links back to documents
cues.zh: 他们叫它 Backrub，是因为它利用指向文档的反向链接

cues.en: to decide how credible they are. If lots of pages on the grid are linking to you, then clearly you're important. And then if you link to somebody, that link means they're probably important as well. It's really, really clever.
cues.zh: 来判断这些文档有多可信。如果网格上有很多页面链接到你，那你显然很重要。而如果你链接到某个人，那个链接就说明他可能也很重要。这真的非常非常聪明。

cues.en: And they're bouncing this idea around and thinking,
cues.zh: 他们反复琢磨这个想法，想着：

cues.en: this could really go somewhere. What are we going to call it? And Sergei says, you know, my kid was in school the other day. And they were telling him about this number called a Google, which is the biggest number. It's like 10 followed by a million zeros or something. Maybe we should call our new search engine that because Back Rub sounds a little bit questionable.
cues.zh: 这真的可能大有前途。我们该叫它什么？Sergei 说，你知道，我孩子前几天在学校，他们跟他讲了一个叫 Google 的数，是最大的数。大概是 10 后面跟一百万个零还是什么。也许我们该把新搜索引擎叫这个名字，因为 Back Rub 听起来有点不靠谱。

cues.en: And remember, we haven't been invented yet so no one's going to be able to find us.
cues.zh: 记住，我们还没诞生，所以没人能找到我们。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: they call it Google and they ask someone to go and register the domain. And of course what happens is autocorrect happens
cues.zh: 他们就把它叫作 Google，并让别人去注册域名。当然，接下来发生的是自动更正

cues.en: and they end up with goggle.com.
cues.zh: 结果他们注册成了 goggle.com。

cues.en: Now it's a great idea. You know, the technology works really well. They have this wonderfully minimalist
cues.zh: 这个想法很棒。你知道，这项技术运行得非常好。他们有一个非常极简的

cues.en: home page. Everyone else is plastering as much advertising as they can onto their grid portals. Goggle has this really nice stripped down page, but there is just one problem.
cues.zh: 主页。其他人都在往自己的门户网格上尽可能多地贴广告。Google 有一个非常简洁的页面，但只有一个问题。

cues.en: They have no idea how they are ever going to make any money out of something that works well, is minimalist, and they are providing for free.
cues.zh: 他们完全不知道如何从一个运行良好、极简且免费提供的东西上赚钱。

cues.en: And so they start kind of looking around for a business plan. And someone suggests maybe you could run advertising. They didn't like that idea at all.
cues.zh: 于是他们开始四处寻找商业模式。有人建议也许可以做广告。他们一点也不喜欢这个想法。

cues.en: And then Larry Page takes a call.
cues.zh: 然后 Larry Page 接了一个电话。

cues.en: It's Steve Jobs. He's working on something, something big, something secret.
cues.zh: 是 Steve Jobs。他正在做某件事，一件大事，一件秘密的事。

cues.en: He might be interested in acquiring Goggle's PageRank technology.
cues.zh: 他可能有意收购 Google 的 PageRank 技术。

cues.en: Now
cues.zh: 那么

cues.en: we don't know exactly what took place next. We don't know what was discussed in those meetings. We don't know who paid who for what or how much. But we know what happened after that.
cues.zh: 我们不知道接下来到底发生了什么。我们不知道那些会议里讨论了什么。我们不知道谁付了谁多少钱、为了什么。但我们知道之后发生了什么。

cues.en: Computer journalists,
cues.zh: 计算机记者们，

cues.en: April 1999, everyone is talking about the Millennium Bug. We're all going to get killed on the stroke of midnight by all these nuclear missiles that can't handle four digit dates or whatever.
cues.zh: 1999 年 4 月，所有人都在谈论千年虫问题。我们都会在午夜钟声敲响时被那些处理不了四位年份的核导弹之类的东西干掉。

cues.en: There is a break from the Millennium Bug hysteria when all of the computer journalists in Silicon Valley get into work one day. And on their desk, they find a hand delivered black envelope.
cues.zh: 然后千年虫的恐慌出现了中断——有一天，硅谷所有的计算机记者来上班时，在桌上发现了一个专人递送的黑色信封。

cues.en: They open it up and inside there is a card, black printed card. On the front, it just says, get ready for the next generation.
cues.zh: 他们打开盒子，里面有一张卡片，是黑色印刷卡片。正面只写着：“准备迎接下一代。”

cues.en: On the back, Menlo Park Amphitheater,
cues.zh: 背面写着：门洛帕克圆形剧场，

cues.en: They immediately think this must be a Star Wars thing. May the fourth be with you. So someone phones Lucasfilm. Lucasfilm said, don't be ridiculous. Why would anyone make a sequel to Star Wars?
cues.zh: 他们立刻觉得这一定和《星球大战》有关。愿原力与你同在。于是有人打电话给 Lucasfilm。Lucasfilm 说：“别开玩笑了。谁会想给《星球大战》拍续集？”

cues.en: We
cues.zh: 我们

cues.en: are not going to mess with perfection.
cues.zh: 可不会去糟蹋完美。

cues.en: And the rumor mill starts working overtime. What is it? Why are we going? What is this next generation thing? What are we talking about?
cues.zh: 谣言顿时满天飞。这到底是什么？我们为什么要去？所谓的下一代又是什么？我们在说什么？

cues.en: On the day May 4 comes around, the Menlo Park Amphitheater is the auditorium is packed. A little before nine a. M, hush falls over the audience. Steve Jobs takes the stage. And he talks for a while. He talks about the grid. He talks about digital publishing, about empowering people, about technology, about the social impact of all of the technology.
cues.zh: 5月4日当天，门洛帕克圆形剧场，也就是礼堂，座无虚席。上午9点还没到，观众席便安静下来。Steve Jobs 走上舞台，讲了好一会儿。他谈到电网、数字出版、赋能大众、技术，以及所有这些技术带来的社会影响。

cues.en: And just as everyone wonders where he's going with this, he reaches behind his podium and he pulls out
cues.zh: 就在大家都纳闷他接下来要说什么时，他伸手到讲台后面，拿出了

cues.en: is
cues.zh: 这

cues.en: that a laptop?
cues.zh: 难道是台笔记本电脑？

cues.en: It's called the Nextbook.
cues.zh: 它叫 Nextbook。

cues.en: Nobody's ever seen anything quite like it. It's less than an inch thick. It's machined from a single piece of aluminum. It's anodized lustrous black. It's got no floppy disk drive. It's got no CD ROM drive. It's got no serial port. How do you plug your printer in? And they're going, you don't need printers. This is the future.
cues.zh: 以前没人见过这样的东西。它不到一英寸厚，由一整块铝材切削而成，表面经过阳极氧化处理，呈现出亮泽的黑色。它没有软盘驱动器，没有 CD-ROM 驱动器，也没有串口。打印机要怎么接？他们的回答是：“你不需要打印机。这就是未来。”

cues.en: It's got two USB ports and a headphone jack. Questions start buzzing through the crowd. How do you connect that to anything? How do I get my games? How do I run SimCity? It doesn't have a floppy disk drive. And that's when he unveils his masterstroke because throughout the audience, there are plants. About two dozen Apple employees reach under their seats and they pull out their Nextbooks, they open the lid,
cues.zh: 它有两个 USB 接口和一个耳机插孔。人群里开始议论纷纷：这玩意儿怎么连任何东西？我怎么把游戏弄进去？我怎么运行 SimCity？它连软驱都没有。就在这时，他亮出了绝招，因为观众席里安排了托儿。大约二十几名 Apple 员工把手伸到座位底下，掏出他们的 Nextbooks，打开上盖，

cues.en: and they are already playing the live video stream of Jobs on stage doing his presentation.
cues.zh: 而他们已经在播放 Jobs 在台上做演示的实时视频流。

cues.en: Nobody has seen WiFi before. Nobody has seen streaming video before. Nobody's seen a laptop like this before. They forget they're supposed to be journalists. People are elbowing each other in the face and clambering over seats trying to get a look at this thing. They are so blown away that they completely forget they're supposed to be there writing about this thing because nobody has ever seen anything like it.
cues.zh: 以前没人见过 WiFi。没人见过流媒体视频。没人见过这样的笔记本电脑。他们忘了自己本该是记者。人们互相用手肘顶对方的脸，爬过座位想看一眼这东西。他们被震撼到完全忘了自己本该在那里写关于这东西的报道，因为从来没人见过这样的东西。

cues.en: It's the fastest, lightest laptop the world has ever seen. Three thirty three megahertz ARM RISC processor,
cues.zh: 这是世界上见过的最快、最轻的笔记本电脑。333 MHz ARM RISC 处理器，

cues.en: 64 megabytes of RAM, five gigs
cues.zh: 64 MB 内存，5 GB

cues.en: of flash drive space.
cues.zh: 闪存空间。

cues.en: It's got the next version of the next step operating system built into it. It has built in wireless internet. It ships with a box called the Nextender, a thing about the size of a hardback book. You plug this in your phone jack. It's got a CD ROM drive in it. It supplies the wireless networking for your house so you don't need to sit next to a phone jack every time you're doing anything. And,
cues.zh: 它内置了下一代 Next Step 操作系统。它内置无线互联网。它附带一个叫 Nextender 的盒子，大概一本精装书那么大。你把它插进电话插孔。里面有一个 CD-ROM 驱动器。它为你的房子提供无线网络，这样你每次用的时候就不必坐在电话插孔旁边。而且，

cues.en: of course,
cues.zh: 当然，

cues.en: Next Step ships with its own brand new grid browser.
cues.zh: Next Step 还自带全新的 Grid 浏览器。

cues.en: We say brand new. It's called Nexus.
cues.zh: 我们说全新的。它叫 Nexus。

cues.en: And the DNA of Nexus goes all the way back to the very first GridBrowser.
cues.zh: 而 Nexus 的 DNA 可以一路追溯到最早的 GridBrowser。

cues.en: Application
cues.zh: 应用程序

cues.en: developed by Tim Berners Lee on the Next operating system a decade earlier.
cues.zh: 由 Tim Berners Lee 十年前在 Next 操作系统上开发。

cues.en: It's responsive.
cues.zh: 它是响应式的。

cues.en: It's got the fastest hyperlisp interpreter anyone's ever seen. It's wired right into the fabric of the new operating system.
cues.zh: 它拥有前所未见的最快 hyperlisp 解释器。它直接接入新操作系统的底层结构。

cues.en: And the whole thing is seamlessly integrated with Goggle search technology.
cues.zh: 而且整个东西与 Goggle 搜索技术无缝集成。

cues.en: You can bring up a window. You can search for what you're looking for. It doesn't matter if it's in your folders, in your backups, in your mail, if it's on the grid somewhere.
cues.zh: 你可以打开一个窗口。你可以搜索你要找的东西。不管它在你的文件夹里、备份里、邮件里，还是在网格上的某个地方。

cues.en: It will find it for you. Steve Jobs is back with a bang.
cues.zh: 它会帮你找到。Steve Jobs 强势回归。

cues.en: The next generation has arrived.
cues.zh: 下一代已经到来。

cues.en: The millennium bug comes and goes. The missiles do not go off. Nobody dies, but we all wake up with one hell of a hangover.
cues.zh: 千年虫来了又走了。导弹没有发射。没有人死掉，但我们醒来时都宿醉得厉害。

cues.en: And the next generation of computing looks like this. We have Steve Jobs, the Next Corporation, the next book running Nexus based on Tim Berners Lee's operating system. We've got the banana boxes running Blink, the browser they got out of the Norwegian telephone company Telenor.
cues.zh: 而下一代计算看起来是这样的。我们有 Steve Jobs、Next 公司、运行 Nexus 的下一代产品，基于 Tim Berners Lee 的操作系统。我们有香蕉盒子运行 Blink，这是他们从挪威电话公司 Telenor 拿到的浏览器。

cues.en: We've got Gen95
cues.zh: 我们有 Gen95

cues.en: and Perfect Digital going all the way back to Cello invented by a librarian working in a law school.
cues.zh: 还有 Perfect Digital，一路追溯到 Cello，由一位在法学院工作的图书管理员发明。

cues.en: And we've got some microsystems who for some reason are still hanging around going, we can run NCSA Mosaic. Look, it supports Java, which nobody cares. But they've invested heavily in their marketing and they're going to keep plugging away at it.
cues.zh: 我们还有一些 microsystems，不知为何还在徘徊，说我们能运行 NCSA Mosaic。看，它支持 Java，但没人在乎。不过他们在营销上投入巨大，还会继续死磕下去。

cues.en: A couple years later,
cues.zh: 几年后，

cues.en: the buzz starts.
cues.zh: 热潮开始涌动。

cues.en: Nintendo are coming up with something big. Now nobody's heard very much from them since John Carmack and Romero and Jim Clark and Mark Anderson all went off to Seattle with Nintendo bankrolling whatever they wanted to come up with. They did ship a very successful Super Mario Quake World.
cues.zh: 任天堂正在酝酿大动作。自从John Carmack、Romero、Jim Clark和Mark Anderson跑到西雅图，任天堂出资支持他们想做的任何东西之后，就很少有人听到他们的消息了。他们确实推出了一款非常成功的Super Mario Quake World。

cues.en: But after that, everything goes a bit quiet. December 2002, just in time for Christmas, Nintendo unveiled a platform that they think is going to change the world.
cues.zh: 但之后，一切都安静了下来。2002年12月，正好赶在圣诞节前，任天堂揭晓了一个他们认为将改变世界的平台。

cues.en: And it's just called reality.
cues.zh: 它的名字就叫现实。

cues.en: It is a massively multiplayer online world. An immersive three d experience
cues.zh: 这是一个大型多人在线世界。沉浸式三维体验

cues.en: takes the world by storm. It's John Carmack and John Romero's dream of implementing the metaverse visualized by Neal Stephenson in his books or The Matrix from William Gibson's Neuromancer books.
cues.zh: 席卷全球。这是John Carmack和John Romero实现元宇宙的梦想，由Neal Stephenson在他的书中构想，或是William Gibson《神经漫游者》系列中的《黑客帝国》。
